chief_complaint: Persistent fatigue, brain fog, and disrupted sleep

transcript_segments.speaker: provider
transcript_segments.text: Good morning. What would you most like us to focus on today?

transcript_segments.speaker: patient
transcript_segments.text: For about six months I have felt exhausted even after a full night in bed. By midafternoon I have brain fog and struggle to finish work.

transcript_segments.speaker: provider
transcript_segments.text: Did this begin suddenly, and what makes it better or worse?

transcript_segments.speaker: patient
transcript_segments.text: It built gradually after a very stressful project. Coffee helps briefly, but I crash later. A short walk usually clears my head a little.

transcript_segments.speaker: provider
transcript_segments.text: Tell me about sleep, including how long you sleep and whether you wake during the night.

transcript_segments.speaker: patient
transcript_segments.text: I go to bed around 10:30, wake near 2 or 3 most nights, and often take an hour to fall back asleep. I average about six hours and wake unrefreshed.

transcript_segments.speaker: provider
transcript_segments.text: Any snoring, morning headaches, chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting, fever, or unexplained weight loss?

transcript_segments.speaker: patient
transcript_segments.text: My partner says I snore occasionally, but there have been no witnessed pauses. No morning headaches, chest pain, breathing trouble, fainting, fever, or weight loss.

transcript_segments.speaker: provider
transcript_segments.text: Walk me through meals, hydration, exercise, medicines, and supplements.

transcript_segments.speaker: patient
transcript_segments.text: Breakfast is often just coffee. Lunch may be late, then I crave something sweet around 3. I drink about four glasses of water. I walk twice a week. I take levothyroxine 50 micrograms every morning, magnesium glycinate 200 milligrams at night, and vitamin D3 2,000 international units daily. No medication allergies.

transcript_segments.speaker: provider
transcript_segments.text: Are you taking the levothyroxine separately from food and supplements?

transcript_segments.speaker: patient
transcript_segments.text: I take it with coffee and usually take magnesium about twenty minutes later. I did not realize they should be separated.

transcript_segments.speaker: provider
transcript_segments.text: Your synthetic demonstration labs from last week show TSH 4.8, free T4 0.9, ferritin 24, vitamin D 31, fasting glucose 102, and hemoglobin 13.1. Your thyroid exam today is normal. Blood pressure is 118 over 74, pulse 72, temperature 98.2, and weight 154 pounds.

transcript_segments.speaker: patient
transcript_segments.text: Could the timing of my thyroid medicine be part of this? My mother also has hypothyroidism.

transcript_segments.speaker: provider
transcript_segments.text: It may contribute because coffee, food, and magnesium can reduce absorption, but the fatigue is likely multifactorial. Sleep fragmentation, inconsistent meals, low hydration, borderline iron stores, and workload stress are also relevant.

transcript_segments.speaker: provider
transcript_segments.text: Take levothyroxine with water on an empty stomach and wait 30 to 60 minutes before coffee or food. Separate magnesium by at least four hours. Continue the current dose until we repeat TSH and free T4 in six weeks.

transcript_segments.speaker: provider
transcript_segments.text: For the next month, eat a protein-containing breakfast, avoid skipping lunch, increase water gradually toward eight glasses daily, and take a ten-minute walk after lunch on at least five days each week. Continue magnesium and vitamin D at current doses.

transcript_segments.speaker: provider
transcript_segments.text: We will also order a complete blood count, ferritin with iron studies, B12, folate, comprehensive metabolic panel, and repeat thyroid labs. Keep a two-week sleep and energy log. If snoring worsens or pauses are witnessed, we will consider a sleep evaluation. Follow up in six weeks, sooner for chest pain, fainting, shortness of breath, or rapidly worsening symptoms.

transcript_segments.speaker: patient
transcript_segments.text: That feels manageable. I will change the medication timing and start the log today.
